name: Retail

summary: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation are the volume use cases.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Business Outlook Survey places retail trade AI adoption at 15.5 percent, a figure that held steady across the two most recent reporting periods, suggesting the sector has reached a plateau in early mainstream uptake rather than continuing rapid acceleration. That number reflects firms answering yes to having used AI in the prior two weeks, so it captures active operational use rather than experimentation or planned investment.

Retail AI deployments cluster around a few high-value problems. Demand forecasting, product recommendation engines, and customer-service automation represent the core use cases that NRF, Coresight, and IHL each flag as priority areas for the sector. The National Retail Federation highlights store automation, inventory computer vision, and customer-experience software as the categories where adoption tracking is most developed, and NRF notes that digital pricing tools are gaining traction as suited to fast-moving, competitive conditions.

At the company level, the deployments being reported span both footwear and apparel. Per IHL Group, Boot Barn's fiscal first quarter of 2027 showed ecommerce sales growing 13.4 percent, with growth attributed in part to intent-aware discovery and agentic AI tools that improved search relevance and preserved brand voice across channels. IHL also reports that Crocs signed a ten-year strategic agreement with Infosys to deploy AI-first solutions across enterprise IT and business operations, with the stated aims of unifying data, breaking down silos, and enabling real-time decision-making.

Inventory inefficiency remains a significant backdrop to these investments. IHL Group reports that inventory distortion has fallen to 1.7 trillion dollars globally, yet empty shelves still cost 690.9 billion dollars, a figure that frames why AI agents focused on stock availability are attracting sustained attention. Coresight Research, which focuses on retail and technology and runs a forum exploring AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-facing businesses, identifies merchandising and supply-chain logistics as the areas where AI market sizing is most active.

The sourced material does not provide specific ROI benchmarks, regulatory findings, or risk disclosures for the sector, so readers should treat the operational examples above as directional rather than representative. What the data collectively suggest for a retailer evaluating deployment is that the technology is genuinely in use at scale, that the near-term payoff cases involve search relevance, inventory visibility, and pricing efficiency, and that long-horizon commitments such as Crocs' ten-year Infosys agreement indicate some large operators are treating AI infrastructure as a core operational bet rather than a tactical add-on.
